land.text: Tokharistan, ruled from Kunduz by the Yabghus

capitals.name: Suyab (Ak-Beshim), also Ordukent
capitals.note: 'the principal capital' in the Chu valley east of Bishkek (WTK page). Summer seat: Navekat, 'near Tashkent' under Tong Yabghu (winter capital Suyab); Istami's winter camp was near Karashar. Coordinates are the gazetteer's for Suyab.

rulers.name: Tardu
rulers.note: Page table 576-603 (infobox) or 575-603 (text); khagan of the united khaganate from 599 (Tardu page); Niri Qaghan is listed as 587-604 (infobox) beside him.

rulers.name: Tong Yabghu Qaghan
rulers.note: Table 618-628, text 618-630; the Tong Yabghu page has the murder 'c. 630', infobox 628.

rulers.name: Kulug Sibir

rulers.note: Text 642-651; enthroned by Taizong's backing (Tang campaigns page).

rulers.name: Ashina Helu
rulers.note: Reign 651-658 on the page; beaten on the Irtysh in 657, pardoned in 658, died in Chang'an in 659 (Ashina Helu page).

keyframe_review.note: 587-591, 3.26 M km2. The shape is the 592 shape plus about 480 cells (0.12 M km2) south of the Oxus (Balkh, Badghis, Herat). Tokhara Yabghus page: in 588-589 the Turks briefly took Balkh, Talaqan, Badghis and Herat before Bahram Chobin drove them back, and the earlier attacks of 569-570 on the Sasanian-held principalities south of the Oxus 'apparently did not permanently occupy' them; so the southern strip is a 588-589 contest zone (ledger), not Western Turk land for all five years. Turfan and Hami come out as the allied oasis of Gaochang (ledger, vassal events), not as direct land.

correction.text: the 592 shape (the realm north of the Oxus, from the Tarim to the Caspian) without Turfan-Hami; the land south of the Oxus is contested 588-589 and otherwise Sasanian

keyframe_review.note: 592-601, 3.12 M km2: Tardu's and Niri Qaghan's western realm; the page's only extent for this age is Istami's winter camp near Karashar and a border drawn along the Oxus in 571. Turfan-Hami (Gaochang) taken out as an allied oasis, not direct land (see 587 and the Gaochang vassal events). 599-603 Tardu's claim on the eastern half is a contest in the ledger, not a change of this shape.

602-625, 3.86 M km2: the 592 shape plus 0.64 M km2 of the Tarim Basin (2,019 of its 3,723 cells; the rest within 35-119 cells each in Dzungaria, Bactria, Ferghana, Chu-Ili). Tarim Basin page: before the Tang campaigns the oasis states were 'then vassals of the Western Turkic Khaganate' (no year, no named governors); so the Tarim is vassal tint, not direct colour (rule 4). The year 602 is Cliopatria's. The page-silent bridge is a confidence-1 vassal_start.

correction.text: the 602 shape without the Tarim Basin and Turfan-Hami, which are vassal oases of the khaganate (Tarim Basin page: 'then vassals of the Western Turkic Khaganate')

keyframe_review.note: 626 only, 3.85 M km2: the 602 shape within 34 cells. WTK page: Tong Yabghu (618-630) ruled 'from the Tarim basin to the Caspian Sea'. From 625 the shape also holds Tokharistan south of the Oxus (Tokhara Yabghus page: 'In 625, Tong Yabgu invaded Tokharistan'), which Cliopatria leaves out. Overlap noted on the return pass: the added Tokharistan (intersect Bactria and Afghanistan, 375 cells) lies under 305 cells of Karkota Dynasty 626 and 34 of Turk Shahis 626. It stays here because the Tokhara Yabghus page backs it ('In 625, Tong Yabgu invaded Tokharistan'); the Karkota cells are Cliopatria's error and the Turk Shahis and Rashidun cells need sa-03 and me-07 to act (dossier notes, 'Tokharistan overlap').

correction.text: the 626 shape without the Tarim Basin and Turfan-Hami (vassal oases), plus Tokharistan south of the Oxus (Kunduz), where Tardush Shad was installed in 625

keyframe_review.note: 627 only, 4.19 M km2: the 626 shape plus 1,250 cells, the Caucasus (Caucasian Albania 343 cells, Transcaucasia 325, Dagestan 85, Iberia 63), the Pontic steppe (440) and the Volga (182). Third Perso-Turkic War page: in early 627 Göktürk and Khazar forces took Derbent and sacked Aghvania, then besieged Tbilisi. The Caucasus part is the campaign. The Pontic and Volga part is not land the page puts under direct Turkic rule: Tong Yabghu page, Bori Shad was likely commander of the Khazars, 'the westernmost vassal tribes'; the 630 clients (Khazars, Great Bulgaria) are vassal events in the ledger. Overlap noted on the return pass: the added Tokharistan (intersect Bactria and Afghanistan, 375 cells) lies under 305 cells of Karkota Dynasty 627 and 34 of Turk Shahis. It stays here because the Tokhara Yabghus page backs it ('In 625, Tong Yabgu invaded Tokharistan'); the Karkota cells are Cliopatria's error and the Turk Shahis and Rashidun cells need sa-03 and me-07 to act (dossier notes, 'Tokharistan overlap').

correction.text: the 627 shape without the Pontic and Volga steppe (vassal tribes), the Tarim Basin and Turfan-Hami (vassal oases); the Caucasus campaign land (Aghvania, Iberia, Dagestan) and Tokharistan kept

correction.text: the 628 shape without the Pontic and Volga steppe (vassal tribes), the Tarim Basin and Turfan-Hami (vassal oases); the Caucasus campaign land (Aghvania, Iberia, Dagestan) and Tokharistan kept

Overlap noted on the return pass: the added Tokharistan (intersect Bactria and Afghanistan, 375 cells) lies under 305 cells of Karkota Dynasty 629 and 34 of Turk Shahis. correction.text: the 629 shape without the Pontic and Volga steppe (vassal tribes), the Tarim Basin and Turfan-Hami (vassal oases); the Caucasus campaign land (Aghvania, Iberia, Dagestan, Armenia) and Tokharistan kept

keyframe_review.note: 630-632, 3.85 M km2, the 626 shape again. Infobox area 3.5 M km2 in 630 (WTK page) against 3.85 M km2: ratio 1.10, fine. Tong Yabghu page: after his murder 'the might of the Western Göktürks largely collapsed' and client tribes such as the Khazars and Great Bulgaria became independent; the Caucasus is given back (Arab-Khazar wars page: Sasanian influence returned by 632). Overlap noted on the return pass: the added Tokharistan (intersect Bactria and Afghanistan, 375 cells) lies under 305 cells of Karkota Dynasty and 34 of Turk Shahis. It stays here because the Tokhara Yabghus page backs it ('In 625, Tong Yabgu invaded Tokharistan'); the Karkota cells are Cliopatria's error and the Turk Shahis and Rashidun cells need sa-03 and me-07 to act (dossier notes, 'Tokharistan overlap').

correction.text: the 630 shape without the Tarim Basin and Turfan-Hami (vassal oases), plus Tokharistan south of the Oxus

keyframe_review.note: 633-640, 3.85 M km2, identical to 630. Rulers per the page's table: Duolu Qaghan 633-634, Ishbara Tolis 634-639; the Turfan oasis (Gaochang) falls to the Tang in 640. Overlap noted on the return pass: the added Tokharistan (intersect Bactria and Afghanistan, 375 cells) lies under 305 cells of Karkota Dynasty and 34 of Turk Shahis. correction.text: the 633 shape without the Tarim Basin and Turfan-Hami, plus Tokharistan

keyframe_review.note: 641-643, 3.86 M km2, +2 cells. Tang campaigns page: Taizong annexed Gaochang in 640, so Turfan-Hami cannot stay in the shape; in 641 he backed Isbara Yabghu, and Tu-lu Qaghan 'assassinated his rival and unified the Western Turkic Khaganate'; in 642 Taizong enthroned Irbis Seguy. Overlap noted on the return pass: the added Tokharistan (intersect Bactria and Afghanistan, 375 cells) lies under 305 cells of Karkota Dynasty and 34 of Turk Shahis. It stays here because the Tokhara Yabghus page backs it ('In 625, Tong Yabgu invaded Tokharistan'); the Karkota cells are Cliopatria's error and the Turk Shahis and Rashidun cells need sa-03 and me-07 to act (dossier notes, 'Tokharistan overlap').

correction.text: the 641 shape without the Tarim Basin and Turfan-Hami (annexed by the Tang in 640), plus Tokharistan

keyframe_review.note: 644-646, 3.86 M km2. Tang campaigns page: Karasahr fell to the Tang in 644 and was lost again to a usurper backed by Kucha and the Western Turks; the Tang retook it in 648 and Kucha on 19 January 649. Overlap noted on the return pass: the added Tokharistan (intersect Bactria and Afghanistan, 375 cells) lies under 305 cells of Karkota Dynasty, 320 of Turk Shahis 644-665 and 19 of Rashidun Caliphate 644. It stays here because the Tokhara Yabghus page backs it ('In 625, Tong Yabgu invaded Tokharistan'); the Karkota cells are Cliopatria's error and the Turk Shahis and Rashidun cells need sa-03 and me-07 to act (dossier notes, 'Tokharistan overlap').

correction.text: the 644 shape without the Tarim Basin and Turfan-Hami (vassal oases or Tang), plus Tokharistan

keyframe_review.note: 647-655, 1.30 M km2. The shape loses everything north of the Tian Shan at once (Dzungaria 82% of its cells, Semirechye 78%, Kazakh Steppe 58%, Altai 44%) and keeps Transoxiana, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and the western Tarim; no opened page supports that. Ashina Helu page: he rose against Irbis Seguy in 646, fled to the Tang in 648, returned and in the 650s was khagan with Suyab and Chach in his orbit; Tang campaigns page: he declared himself qaghan, unified the Western Turks and raided the Tarim; the Western Turks still held the steppe when Su Dingfang beat them at the Irtysh River in 657. So the northern steppe stays Western Turk land to 657, minus the Tarim. Return pass: the first version put the whole 644 shape back and so drew 114 cells (28,800 km2; 96 in the Kazakh Steppe, bbox 52.6-54.5 E, 45.4-48.2 N) that Cliopatria's Khazaria 647 shape holds for 647-657 twice. They are now taken out (minus Khazaria 647) and leave through a 647 loss to khazaria (ledger). The Khazars page dates no step of the Khazar growth, so the handover year is Cliopatria's. Overlap noted on the return pass: the added Tokharistan (intersect Bactria and Afghanistan, 375 cells) lies under 305 cells of Karkota Dynasty (to 655), 320 of Turk Shahis and 19 of Rashidun Caliphate. It stays here because the Tokhara Yabghus page backs it ('In 625, Tong Yabgu invaded Tokharistan'); the Karkota cells are Cliopatria's error and the Turk Shahis and Rashidun cells need sa-03 and me-07 to act (dossier notes, 'Tokharistan overlap').

correction.text: the 644 shape (the full realm from the Altai and the Irtysh to Transoxiana and Tokharistan) without the Tarim Basin and Turfan-Hami, which the Tang took by 649, and without the 114 cells of the Ural steppe that Cliopatria hands to Khazaria in 647, kept to 657 (years 647-655), plus Tokharistan

keyframe_review.note: 656-660, 1.27 M km2. Tang campaigns page: Su Dingfang defeated Helu on the Irtysh in 657 and 'the remaining tribes of the Western Turks surrendered'; the Tang 'had reached its largest extent'. The khaganate ends in 657 (WTK page: 'destroyed the khaganate in 657-659'; proxies Buzhen and Mishe were installed under Tang jimi rule). The shape holds for 656-657 as the 644 shape without the Tarim; 658-660 are not Western Turk land (Tang dossier gains Dzungaria and Semirechye in 657). Return pass: the 114 cells that Khazaria holds from 647 are also taken out here (minus Khazaria 647), so the two states do not overlap in 656-657. Overlap noted on the return pass: the added Tokharistan (intersect Bactria and Afghanistan, 375 cells) lies under 1 cell of Karkota Dynasty 656, 320 of Turk Shahis and 19 of Rashidun Caliphate. It stays here because the Tokhara Yabghus page backs it ('In 625, Tong Yabgu invaded Tokharistan'); the Karkota cells are Cliopatria's error and the Turk Shahis and Rashidun cells need sa-03 and me-07 to act (dossier notes, 'Tokharistan overlap').

correction.text: for 656-657 only: the 644 shape without the Tarim Basin, Turfan-Hami and the 114 cells that Khazaria holds from 647, plus Tokharistan; no state from 658

region.text: the western Goktürk realm ruled from Suyab, the Chu valley, from the Tarim to the Caspian steppe

ledger.note: 587: the western half of the Goktürks stands as its own khaganate under Tardu and Niri Qaghan. Infobox: 'Administrative region of the First Turkic Khaganate (581-603); Independent empire (603-657)'; the table gives Niri Qaghan 587-604 and Tardu 576-603; Cliopatria starts the state in 587 and the page has no founding year ('Within 35 years' the two khaganates were independent).

region.text: the Turfan oasis, the Kingdom of Gaochang (Karakhoja)

ledger.note: 587: Turfan and Hami as a Turkic client oasis. The WTK page says only 'Gaochang was conquered in 640' and Tang campaigns page that Tu-lu promised Karakhoja (Gaochang) military support in 638; Cliopatria draws the oasis as Western Goktürk land from 587, so the start year is its, not a page's. Gaochang page (re-read): the Qu dynasty 'became vassals of the Göktürks' when they emerged as the supreme power, and Qu Wentai later allied with the Western Turks before Hou Junji's 640 campaign; no year for either, so 587 stays Cliopatria's.

region.text: Balkh, Talaqan, Badghis and Herat, south of the Oxus

ledger.note: 588: the Turks cross the Oxus. under Bagha Qaghan the Turks briefly took Balkh, Talaqan, Badghis and Herat (Tokhara Yabghus page, 588-589); WTK page: 'In 588-589 the Turks were defeated by Persians near Herat'.

region.text: Balkh, Talaqan, Badghis and Herat

ledger.note: 589: Bahram Chobin drives the Turks back over the Oxus; the Oxus line (WTK page: 'In 571 a border was drawn along the Oxus') holds again and the land south of it stays Sasanian. The page gives the war as 588-589, not the month of the retreat.

region.text: the eastern half of the khaganate, Otuken and the Mongolian steppe, which Tardu 'subjugated' after Tulan Qaghan's death

ledger.note: 599: Tardu 'declared himself to be khagan of the united khaganate', claiming the eastern half after Tulan Qaghan's death; 'his new status was not recognised widely' and the campaign he launched against China failed. Cliopatria draws no Western Goktürk land on the Mongolian Plateau, so this is a contest, not a gain.

region.text: the Tarim oasis states Kucha, Karasahr, Kashgar, Khotan

ledger.counterpart: Tarim oasis states (Kucha, Karasahr, Kashgar, Khotan)
ledger.note: 602: the Tarim oasis states as clients. Tarim Basin page: before the Tang campaigns the oasis states were 'then vassals of the Western Turkic Khaganate' (no year, no named governor); WTK page: Istami 'ruled the khaganate from a winter camp near Karashar'. The year is Cliopatria's (its 602 shape adds 2,019 Tarim cells), not a page's. Kucha page (re-read): it never names the Western Turks and dates no overlordship; its infobox has the Tang conquest in 648. 602 stays Cliopatria's.

region.text: the eastern half, no longer claimed from the west

ledger.note: 603: Tardu is gone and the two khaganates are separate for good. The page: 'After a rebellion of his subjects, he disappeared (was likely killed)' in '603 or 604', and the khaganate 'permanently divided in two'; WTK page: Western Turkic Khaganate 'independent empire (603-657)'.

region.text: Tokharistan south of the Oxus, ruled from Kunduz by Tardush Shad

ledger.note: 625: Tong Yabghu takes Tokharistan. 'In 625, Tong Yabgu invaded Tokharistan and forced the Hephthalite principalities to submit' and installed his son Tardush Shad at Kunduz, 'south of the Oxus'. Cliopatria draws nothing south of the Oxus after 591. Overlap noted on the return pass: these 375 cells lie under Cliopatria's Karkota Dynasty 626-655 (305 cells), Turk Shahis 561-643 (34) and 644-665 (320) and Rashidun 644 (19); the dossier keeps them as Western Turk land and routes the other shapes to sa-03 and me-07 (notes).

region.text: Derbent, Aghvania (Caucasian Albania) and Tbilisi (Iberia), as far as the 627 shape reaches

ledger.note: 627: Turks and Khazars take Derbent and sack Aghvania. in early 627 Göktürk and Khazar forces took Derbent and sacked Aghvania, then besieged Tbilisi; Tong Yabghu planned to incorporate Aghvania into his khaganate rather than only plunder it. Region is the researcher's reading of Derbent, Aghvania and Tbilisi.

region.text: the Khazar country, the Khazars as the khaganate's westernmost vassal tribes

ledger.note: 627: the Khazars fight under Bori Shad, 'the westernmost vassal tribes' (Tong Yabghu page); the Khazar forces besiege Tbilisi (Third Perso-Turkic War page). Cliopatria draws the Khazar country (Dagestan, Terek, lower Volga) as Western Goktürk land in 627-629; the page puts it in the vassal tint. The start year is the campaign's, not the page's. Counterpart is a string, the same in both events: the Khazar state begins in 630, so the khazaria dossier cannot carry a mirror vassal event.

region.text: the Onogur Bulgars on the Pontic steppe, clients of Tong Yabghu

ledger.note: 627: the Pontic steppe under Great Bulgaria's clients. Tong Yabghu page: after his death client tribes such as the Khazars and Great Bulgaria became independent; Cliopatria draws the Pontic steppe and the Volga as Western Goktürk land in 627-629 and Old Great Bulgaria from 633. The start year is Cliopatria's. Reviewer ia-01-d: confidence 1, the Tong Yabghu page gives no year for the Bulgars' client status. Counterpart is a string, the same in both events: Old Great Bulgaria begins in 633, so its dossier cannot carry a mirror vassal event. Kubrat page (re-read): the eastern Bulgars came under the Western Turkic Khaganate by the end of the 6th century, but no year is given for the Onogurs' client status under Tong Yabghu; 627 stays Cliopatria's first year for the land, confidence 1.

region.text: 'most of Armenia', conquered by Chorpan Tarkhan

ledger.note: 629: Armenia. Chorpan Tarkhan 'conquered most of Armenia' after Tbilisi (WTK page, undated); Third Perso-Turkic War page: in April 630 he destroyed a Persian force under Shahrbaraz in Armenia. Cliopatria adds the Armenian Highlands in 629 (62 cells); the year is its, so confidence 1. Third Perso-Turkic War page (re-read): 'In April 630' Böri Shad sent Chorpan Tarkhan 'to invade Armenia', while the infobox dates the war 627-629 and no year is given for how long the Turks held Armenia; the page therefore contradicts Cliopatria's 629 hold, which is kept (confidence 1) because the shape is drawn that way. If the April 630 date is right, the hold falls in 630 only.

region.text: the Khazar country

ledger.note: 630: Tong Yabghu is murdered by his uncle Kulug Sibir (page: 'c. 630', infobox 628) and the western clients break away: client tribes such as the Khazars and Great Bulgaria became independent (page). The Khazars are a state from 630 in Cliopatria. Counterpart is a string, the same in both events: the Khazar state begins in 630, so the khazaria dossier cannot carry a mirror vassal event.

region.text: the Pontic steppe

ledger.note: 630: the Onogur Bulgars on the Pontic steppe break away (see the Khazar entry); Old Great Bulgaria stands from 633 in Cliopatria and Kubrat's union is dated 'between 630 and 635' on its page. Counterpart is a string, the same in both events: Old Great Bulgaria begins in 633, so its dossier cannot carry a mirror vassal event.

region.text: Aghvania, Iberia and Armenia

ledger.note: 630: the Caucasus is given back. The page gives Tong Yabghu's death as 630 and the collapse that followed; Arab-Khazar wars page: Turkic control extended over Iberia, Albania and Adharbayjan c. 627-632, but Sasanian influence returned by 632. Cliopatria ends the 627-629 shape at 630.

region.text: the Derbent country, held by the Khazars from 630 in Cliopatria

ledger.note: 630: Dagestan (Derbent) passes to the Khazars, whose country Cliopatria draws on the North Caucasus and the Terek from 630. The WTK page names no Khazar holding of Derbent in 630; the year is Cliopatria's. Derbent page (re-read): it dates the Turkic sack of Derbent to 627 and the Arab capture to 643 but gives no year for a Khazar hold of Derbent or Dagestan.

region.text: the Turfan oasis (Gaochang)

ledger.note: 640: Gaochang falls. 'Gaochang was conquered in 640' (WTK page); Tang campaigns page: Taizong's forces campaigned 'against Gaochang in 640' and annexed it. The Tang dossier gains the oasis from the Kingdom of Gaochang.

region.text: the Ural steppe north-east of the Caspian (west Kazakhstan, 52.6-54.5 E, 45.4-48.2 N) that Khazaria holds from 647

ledger.note: 647: 114 cells (about 28,800 km2, 96 of them in the Kazakh Steppe) pass from Cliopatria's Western Göktürks 646 shape to its Khazaria 647 shape; the Khazars page has the khaganate dominating c. 650-965 'from the Volga-Don steppes' but dates no step and names no Western Turk loss, so the year and the land are Cliopatria's. Mirror of khazaria's 647 gain from western-gokturks.

region.text: Kucha, Karasahr, Kashgar, Khotan: the Four Garrisons of Anxi

ledger.counterpart: Tarim oasis states (Kucha, Karasahr, Kashgar, Khotan)
ledger.note: 648: the northern Tarim oases pass to the Tang. Tang campaigns page: Karasahr taken in 644 and again in 648 (Ashina She'er; a garrison was set up, the first of the Four Garrisons of Anxi); Kucha 'surrendered on 19 January 649'. Kashgar and Khotan had 'submitted to the Tang' as tributaries in 632 (same page). The Tang dossier gains the Tarim Basin in 648.

region.text: the Tarim oasis states and the Four Garrisons of Anxi

ledger.note: 648: the Tarim goes to the Tang (the clients' land, hatched out of the khaganate's tint); matching the Tang dossier's 648 gain from this state.

region.text: the Western Turks' lands north of the Tian Shan and in the Chu and Ili valleys (Suyab)

ledger.note: 657: the steppe goes to the Tang. Su Dingfang defeated Helu's reported 100,000 cavalry at the Irtysh River, Helu was 'sent to the Tang capital as a prisoner' and 'the remaining tribes of the Western Turks surrendered'; the Tang 'had reached its largest extent'. Matches the Tang dossier's 657 gain of Dzungaria and Semirechye.

region.text: Tokharistan, ruled from Kunduz by the Yabghus

ledger.note: 657: Tokharistan is left to its Yabghus under Tang suzerainty. 'After 650, the Yabghus came, at least partially, under Tang suzerainty'; the page says the Western Turkic Khaganate 'was destroyed by the Tang dynasty in 657 CE' and Kunduz became the Yuezhi Commandery of the Anxi Protectorate. The Yabghus of Tokharistan need a dossier of their own.

region.text: Sogdia, Chach and Ferghana

ledger.note: 657: the Sogdian cities and the Ferghana and Chach oases, drawn by Cliopatria as Western Goktürk land to 660, are left to their princes (Helu fled to Chach, whose ruler Yixian Tarkhan handed him over, Ashina Helu page). The Tang dossier takes them as clients from 661. Protectorate General to Pacify the West page (re-read): in 658 the Grand Protectorate took the governorship of the former Western Turkic lands, and 'in 659 Sogdia, Ferghana, Tashkent, Bukhara, Samarkand, Balkh, Herat, Kashmir, the Pamirs, Tokharistan and Kabul' submitted to it; the page does not mention 661 or the Sixteen Prefectures, so the Tang dossier's 661 start of client status (ea-04) is two years after this page's 659.

region.text: the steppe between the Aral Sea and the Altai

ledger.note: 657: the Kazakh steppe, the Altai and Khwarezm, left to their tribes. The pages name no successor for the steppe west of the Irtysh (WTK page infobox: 'Succeeded by Turgesh, Oghuz Yabgu State, Khazar Khaganate, Kangar union'); the Turgesh 'took up' the leadership about twenty years later. The Khazaria 647 cells are taken out here: they left in 647. Ashina Buzhen page (re-read): Buzhen was appointed Jiwangjue Khagan in 657 and 'given authority to rule over five Western Turkic tribes'; Mishe was killed by Su Haizheng in 662 and the Shunishi and Basaigan chiefs then submitted to the Tibetan Empire; Buzhen died in 667. The page places neither man relative to the Irtysh and does not name the Nushibi or Duolu lands, so the steppe stays 'nobody' (confidence 1); the proxies' tribes are a Tang-dossier matter.

region.text: the khaganate of Ashina Helu in 656-657, from the Irtysh to Transoxiana and Tokharistan: the corrected 656-657 keyframe

ledger.note: 657: the Western Turkic Khaganate falls. 'The Tang destroyed the khaganate in 657-659': Su Dingfang beat Ashina Helu on the Irtysh in 657 (Helu pardoned in 658, died 659); Gaozong installed Buzhen and Mishe as proxy qaghans under Tang rule. Cliopatria runs the shape to 660. The region is the corrected 656-657 keyframe, not Cliopatria's 656 shape (which includes the Tarim and Turfan oases and the 114 Khazaria cells).

wars.name: Turkic invasion of Bactria and Khorasan
wars.outcome: The Turks briefly took Balkh, Talaqan, Badghis and Herat and were defeated near Herat by Bahram Chobin; the Oxus stays the frontier.
wars.note: WTK page: 'In 588-589 the Turks were defeated by Persians near Herat'. In 591 Bahram Chobin himself fled to the Western Turks.

wars.name: Tardu's bid for the united khaganate

zones.text: the eastern half of the khaganate

wars.outcome: Tardu declared himself khagan of the united khaganate in 599 and was not widely recognised; his campaign against China failed and he vanished in 603 or 604 after a rebellion, leaving the two khaganates permanently divided.
wars.note: The page gives Tardu as yabgu 575-599 and qaghan 599-603 in the infobox but c. 575-603 in the lead.

wars.name: Third Perso-Turkic War
wars.outcome: Göktürk-Byzantine victory (infobox): Derbent and Aghvania sacked, Tbilisi taken after a siege, Chorpan Tarkhan's April 630 ambush in Armenia; Tong Yabghu's murder about 630 ends the Turkic hold on the Caucasus.
wars.note: The page's dates are 627-629; its last dated action is April 630. Heraclius met Tong Yabghu at Tbilisi (Narikala) in 627.

wars.name: Tang campaigns against the Western Turks

zones.text: the steppe north of the Tian Shan and the Chu and Ili valleys, 657

wars.outcome: Tang victory: Gaochang annexed in 640, Karasahr in 644/648, Kucha surrendered 19 January 649, Ashina Helu beaten on the Irtysh in 657 and the khaganate annexed.
wars.note: The page's infobox dates the campaign 640-712; later Western Turk revolts with Tibetan help (670, 677-679) are beyond this state.

certainty.note: Steppe, desert and mountain frontiers throughout; the Oxus line of 571 (WTK page: 'a border was drawn along the Oxus') and the Derbent frontier of 627-630 are the only fixed lines and neither is surveyed. The Tarim and Gaochang oases are tributary tint, whose edge is the oasis, not a line.

notes:
Eastern and Western Goktürks (Cliopatria rows sharing Wikidata Q205466) are two states, not one: WTK page 'Administrative region of the First Turkic Khaganate (581-603); Independent empire (603-657)' and 'Within 35 years' the two were independent; the only joint rule is Tardu's claim of 599-603 (contest in the ledger). This dossier ends the state in 657 (Helu's defeat; page 'destroyed the khaganate in 657-659'), not 660 as Cliopatria does, and the Tang dossier gains Dzungaria and Semirechye in 657 and the Tarim in 648 from this state. Wikipedia field is 'Western Turkic Khaganate' (Cliopatria says 'Göktürks').

Control levels: Cliopatria draws the Tarim Basin (from 602) and Turfan-Hami (from 587) as direct land; the pages give them as vassal oases (Tarim Basin page; Gaochang annexed by the Tang in 640), so the corrected keyframes take them out and the ledger carries two vassal pairs. The Pontic and Volga steppe that Cliopatria adds in 627-629 is taken out as vassal tribes (Khazars, Onogur Bulgars) with vassal pairs 627-630. Tokharistan south of the Oxus (Kunduz) is added from 625 (Cliopatria has none). The 647-660 shape drops the whole northern steppe, which no page supports; the dossier keeps it to 657.

Unverified or thin (page budget 9, used 9): the year of the Tarim and Gaochang vassalage (Cliopatria's, confidence 1); the Armenian conquest year (629, Cliopatria's); what became of the steppe west of the Irtysh and of Sogdia after 657 (pages silent; the Tang dossier has the 661 Sixteen Prefectures); the Navekat summer capital has no coordinates (Tashkent area); no page gave the Western Turks' own 'ten arrows' territory. Not drawn: the Crimea campaign 576-577 and the Volga and North Caucasus lands of 567-576 (west of the 52.4 E edge of every Cliopatria shape before 627; WTK page 'westernmost extent of Turkic power'). Counterparts needing dossiers: tokhara-yabghus (c. 625-758, Kunduz), Kingdom of Gaochang (Qu family) (to 640), the Sogdian city states and Chach, Hephthalite principalities of Tokharistan, Tarim oasis states (Kucha, Karasahr, Kashgar; Kingdom of Khotan exists from 888 in Cliopatria only). Gazetteer: all names used resolve or are listed in the report if not.

Return pass (review ia-01-d, 2026-10-18). (1) Overlap with Khazaria: the 644 shape put back for 647-657 holds 114 cells that Cliopatria's Khazaria 647 shape takes from the Western Göktürks 646 shape; they are now out of the 647-655 and 656-657 keyframes and the 657 dissolve and leave in a 647 loss to khazaria (confidence 1: the year is Cliopatria's; the Khazars page dates no step), with the mirror gain in the khazaria dossier. (2) Tokharistan overlap: the 375 cells of Tokharistan added from 625 (intersect Bactria and Afghanistan) lie under Cliopatria's Karkota Dynasty 626-655 (305 cells), Turk Shahis 561-643 (34) and 644-665 (320) and Rashidun Caliphate 644 (19). Kept, not subtracted, because the Tokhara Yabghus page backs the addition ('In 625, Tong Yabgu invaded Tokharistan'; Tardush Shad at Kunduz). Routing: sa-03 should take the 305 Karkota cells out of karkota-dynasty (the Karkota page names Kashmir, Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, never Balkh or Samangan, and no territory before 700 north of the Hindu Kush); the Tokhara Yabghus page calls the Turk Shahis 'a probable political extension and vassals of the neighbouring Yabghus of Tokharistan' (665-850), so turk-shahis should confine its direct land to Kabul and Kapisa or draw the Bactrian part as vassal tint, and tokhara-yabghus (no Cliopatria row, still needing a dossier) takes the land from 657. me-07 should check the 19 cells of the Rashidun 644 shape: the same page has the Arabs conquering 'the whole of Tokharistan' only in 652-653. This dossier does not shorten the Western Turk hold to 652: the page says the Yabghus' power 'fragmented' after 650 and that Qutaiba had to 're-establish Muslim control over Tokharistan' in 710, but gives no date for an Arab withdrawal, so the 652-653 episode is left open for me-07. (3) Vassal pairs 627-630 now name strings ('Khazar tribes (before the khaganate)', "Onogur Bulgars (before Kubrat's state)") because those dossiers begin in 630 and 633. (4) Thin items re-read with the pages the reviewer named: Gaochang, Kucha, Kubrat, Derbent and Ashina Buzhen are silent on the years (587, 602, 627, 630 and the steppe west of the Irtysh remain Cliopatria's, confidence 1); the Third Perso-Turkic War page puts the Armenian invasion in April 630 where Cliopatria holds Armenia in 629 (kept, flagged in the ledger note: I disagree with the year but the shape stays until another page says how long the Turks held Armenia); the Protectorate General page gives 659 for the submission of Sogdia, Ferghana, Tashkent, Bukhara, Samarkand, Balkh, Herat, Tokharistan and Kabul (the Tang dossier has 661; for ea-04). (5) The 657 dissolve region is now the corrected 656-657 keyframe (10,754 cells). The four 657 losses carry 9,486 of them; the other 1,268 cells (south Kazakhstan 836, Kyrgyzstan 152, Turkmenistan 75, Russia 6 and a few others) leave with the dissolve, whose counterpart is the Tang ('the remaining tribes of the Western Turks surrendered', Tang campaigns page), and the Tang dossier decides in its 657 keyframe whether they are Tang or nobody's.
